statement: A Claude Code plugin is a self-contained directory of components: skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, LSP servers and monitors.
from: A plugin is a self-contained directory of components
to: LSP servers, and monitors.

statement: A plugin manifest (.claude-plugin/plugin.json) is optional: without it Claude Code auto-discovers components in default locations and derives the plugin name from the directory name.
from: The manifest is optional. If omitted,
to: derives the plugin name from the directory name.

statement: A plugin's version is an optional semver string in plugin.json; setting it pins the plugin so users only receive updates when the author bumps it, and if it is also set in the marketplace entry plugin.json wins.
from: version string Optional. Semantic version.
to: If omitted, the version comes from the next source in Version management.

statement: A plugin can declare dependencies on other plugins with semver version constraints.
from: Other plugins this plugin requires, optionally with semver version constraints.
to: Constrain plugin dependency versions

statement: A marketplace is declared by .claude-plugin/marketplace.json at the repository root; each plugin entry needs at minimum a name and a source that tells Claude Code where to fetch it.
locator: Plugin marketplaces, Create the marketplace file
from: Each plugin entry needs at minimum a
to: tells Claude Code where to fetch it from.

statement: A marketplace itself can be pinned to a branch or tag (ref) but not to a sha, while a plugin source listed in the marketplace can be pinned to either ref or exact commit sha.
locator: Plugin marketplaces, Version resolution and release channels
from: Git-based marketplace sources support ref (branch/tag) but not sha.
to: Git-based plugin sources support both ref (branch/tag) and sha (exact commit).

statement: Plugins can also be distributed as npm packages, installed with npm install from the public or a private registry, and pinned with a version or range field.
locator: Plugin marketplaces, Plugin sources, npm packages
from: Plugins distributed as npm packages are installed using npm install.
to: or a private registry your team hosts.

statement: Installing a plugin offers user, project and local scopes; project scope installs for all collaborators on the repository, which adds the plugin to .claude/settings.json.
locator: Discover and install plugins, install scopes
from: Project scope: install for all collaborators on this repository, which adds the plugin to.claude/settings.json
to: Project scope: install for all collaborators on this repository, which adds the plugin to.claude/settings.json

statement: The shared project settings file .claude/settings.json is meant to be committed so teammates get the project's plugins, hooks and environment variables.
locator: Settings files and precedence, scope table
from: Shared project.claude/settings.json
to: the environment variables the project needs

statement: Updating a marketplace-based install is: push changes to the marketplace repository, then users refresh with /plugin marketplace update.
from: Once your marketplace is live, you can update it by pushing changes to your repository.
to: Users refresh their local copy with /plugin marketplace update.

statement: Marketplaces provide centralized discovery, version tracking, automatic updates and multiple source types including git repositories and local paths.
from: Marketplaces provide centralized discovery, version tracking, automatic updates,
to: including git repositories and local paths.

statement: For copied plugins, each installed version is a separate directory in the plugin cache, grouped by marketplace and plugin and named for the resolved version.
from: each installed version is a separate directory in the cache,
to: named for the resolved version

statement: Claude Code's dependency install for plugins is constrained so that no code from the plugin or its packages executes during it, with --ignore-scripts preventing preinstall, install and postinstall scripts.
locator: Plugins reference, plugin caching, dependency install
from: no code from the plugin or its packages executes during it
to: No lifecycle scripts: --ignore-scripts

statement: A local --plugin-dir plugin with the same name as an installed marketplace plugin takes precedence for that session.
from: When a --plugin-dir plugin has the same name as an installed marketplace plugin,
to: the local copy takes precedence for that session.

statement: Claude Code's official guidance for sharing is standalone .claude/ configuration for iteration, converted to a plugin when ready to share.
locator: Create plugins, standalone vs plugins table
from: Start with standalone configuration in.claude/ for quick iteration,
to: then convert to a plugin when you’re ready to share.

statement: A plugin can also live in a skills directory: claude plugin init scaffolds it under ~/.claude/skills and it loads with no marketplace or install step.
from: On the next session it loads as my-tool@skills-dir with no marketplace or install step.
to: On the next session it loads as my-tool@skills-dir with no marketplace or install step.

statement: Unlike a copied marketplace install, a skills-directory plugin is discovered in place rather than copied into the plugin cache.
from: Unlike a copied marketplace install,
to: rather than copied into the plugin cache.

statement: Anthropic's own skills repository is consumed in Claude Code by registering it as a plugin marketplace and installing its plugin(s), not by copying folders.

statement: skills.sh is a third-party Agent Skills directory whose install command is npx skills add <owner/repo>.
